title: Inject an io.Writer dependency
description: Implement a function called Greet that receives two things: a destination to write to and a name. It writes the greeting Hello, followed by the name into that destination and returns nothing. Use the general-purpose "somewhere to write bytes" type for the destination, so the same function works with an in-memory buffer, a network connection, or the terminal: writing with name "Chris" places "Hello, Chris" into the destination. Then implement a second function called GreetToStdout that receives only a name and makes the greeting appear on the program's standard output, by handing Greet the real standard-output stream as its destination: GreetToStdout(name: "Elodie") prints "Hello, Elodie".
objective: Practice dependency injection: write to a general writer interface instead of hard-coding the output, then inject the real standard-output stream so the same function drives the terminal.

title: Capture output with bytes.Buffer
description: A function called Greet is already implemented. It receives a destination to write to and a name, and writes the greeting Hello, followed by the name into that destination: greeting the name "Chris" places "Hello, Chris" there. Write a test for it. Create an in-memory buffer, pass it as the destination along with the name "Chris", then read back the text that was written and check it equals "Hello, Chris". Report a helpful failure that shows what was got versus what was wanted.
objective: Practice testing a function that writes to an injected destination by capturing its output in an in-memory buffer and asserting on the written text.
mutant_hints: greets with the wrong word instead of Hello
adds an extra exclamation mark that should not be there
puts the name before the greeting instead of after it
